source: Hand-written for Terra Tempora; places and dates from standard references (see each event's links).

events.title: Temüjin is born
events.place: Delüün Boldog, on the Onon River (traditional site)
events.summary: The future Genghis Khan is born into the Borjigin clan, son of the chieftain Yesügei. The year is traditionally 1162, though 1155 and 1167 are also given. His father's murder when he was about nine left the family outcast, a hardship that shaped his rise.

events.title: Temüjin proclaimed Genghis Khan
events.place: Great assembly at the source of the Onon River
events.summary: Having united the Mongol and Turkic tribes of the steppe, Temüjin is proclaimed Genghis Khan at a great assembly, a kurultai. He reorganises his people into units of ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand, and lays down the laws later known as the Yassa. The Mongol Empire dates from this moment.

events.title: Siege of Yinchuan
events.place: Zhongxing (Yinchuan), capital of the Western Xia
events.summary: The Mongols besiege the Western Xia capital and try to flood it by diverting the Yellow River, but the dyke breaks and floods their own camp. Emperor Li Anquan submits all the same, paying tribute and giving a daughter in marriage. It is the Mongols' first conquest of a settled state.

events.title: Battle of Yehuling
events.place: Badger's Mouth pass, north-west of Zhangjiakou
events.summary: At the Badger's Mouth pass, Genghis Khan's army destroys a much larger army of the Jin dynasty. The defeat opens northern China to the Mongols and is remembered as one of the bloodiest battles of the age.

events.title: Fall of Zhongdu
events.summary: After the Jin court flees south to Kaifeng, the Mongols take and sack Zhongdu, the Jin capital on the site of today's Beijing. The Jin hold out in the south for almost twenty more years.

events.title: Siege of Otrar
events.summary: The governor of Otrar had massacred a Mongol trade caravan, and the Khwarazm Shah had killed Genghis Khan's envoys. In revenge the Mongols invade Khwarazm and besiege Otrar, which falls after months; its governor is put to death.

events.title: Fall of Bukhara
events.summary: Genghis Khan crosses the Kyzylkum desert to appear behind the Khwarazmian lines and takes Bukhara. The city is sacked and burned; the Persian historian Juvayni has him tell its people that he is the punishment of God.

events.title: Fall of Samarkand
events.place: Samarkand, capital of the Khwarazm Shah
events.summary: Samarkand, the richest city of the Khwarazmian empire, surrenders after a short siege. Much of its garrison is killed and thousands of craftsmen are sent east to work for the Mongols.

events.title: Fall of Gurganj
events.summary: Gurganj, the old Khwarazmian capital, resists for months until the Mongols flood it by breaking the dams of the Amu Darya. Its fall is often counted among the bloodiest massacres in history.

events.title: Battle of the Indus
events.summary: Genghis Khan catches Jalal al-Din, the last Khwarazmian prince, against the Indus and destroys his army. Jalal al-Din escapes by riding his horse off the bank into the river, a feat Genghis Khan is said to have admired.

events.title: Battle of the Kalka River
events.place: Kalka River, north of the Sea of Azov
events.summary: On a long scouting raid around the Caspian, the generals Jebe and Subutai defeat an alliance of Rus princes and Cumans. The captured princes are crushed beneath a wooden platform on which the victors feast.

events.title: Death of Genghis Khan
events.place: Liupan Mountains, during the war on the Western Xia
events.summary: Genghis Khan dies while his armies are destroying the Western Xia; whether from a fall from his horse, illness or a wound is unknown. He is buried in secret in Mongolia, and his grave has never been found.

events.title: Ögedei elected Great Khan
events.summary: At an assembly on the Kherlen River, Genghis Khan's third son Ögedei is confirmed as his successor. Under him the empire builds a capital and a network of relay stations, the yam, and resumes its wars in China, Persia and Europe.

events.title: Fall of the Jin at Caizhou
events.summary: Mongol and Southern Song armies besiege the last Jin emperor at Caizhou. Emperor Aizong hands the throne to a general and takes his own life, and the Jin dynasty ends in 1234.

events.title: Karakorum becomes the capital
events.summary: Ögedei walls Karakorum in the Orkhon valley and makes it the capital. Merchants, envoys and craftsmen from across Eurasia gather there; William of Rubruck later describes its silver tree, a fountain that poured four drinks.

events.title: Sack of Ryazan
events.place: Old Ryazan, on the Oka River
events.summary: Batu and Subutai open the invasion of the Rus principalities by storming Ryazan in December 1237. The city is destroyed and never rebuilt on that site.

events.title: Fall of Vladimir
events.summary: The Mongols take Vladimir, the leading city of north-eastern Rus, in February 1238; the grand prince's family dies in the burning cathedral. A month later Grand Prince Yuri II is killed at the Sit River.

events.title: Fall of Kyiv
events.summary: Kyiv, the old capital of the Rus, falls in December 1240 after a short siege. Most of the city is destroyed, and the Mongols move on into Poland and Hungary.

events.title: Battle of Legnica
events.summary: On 9 April 1241 a Mongol force sent to guard the flank defeats the Polish and Moravian knights of Duke Henry II the Pious, who is killed. Two days later the main army fights at Mohi.

events.title: Battle of Mohi
events.place: Mohi, on the Sajó River, Hungary
events.summary: On the Sajó River, Batu and Subutai crush the army of King Béla IV of Hungary on 11 April 1241. Much of Hungary is ravaged over the following year.

events.title: Death of Ögedei
events.summary: Ögedei dies in December 1241, reportedly after a night of heavy drinking. The princes leading the European campaign turn back for the succession, and the Mongols leave Hungary in 1242.

events.title: Battle of Köse Dağ
events.place: Köse Dağ, between Sivas and Erzincan
events.summary: The general Baiju defeats the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum in eastern Anatolia. The Seljuks become Mongol vassals, paying tribute.

events.title: A papal envoy at Güyük's enthronement
events.place: Sira Ordo, the khan's camp near Karakorum
events.summary: Giovanni da Pian del Carpine, sent by Pope Innocent IV, witnesses Güyük's enthronement as Great Khan. Güyük's reply orders the Pope to come and submit; Carpini's report is one of the first European accounts of the Mongols.

events.title: William of Rubruck at Karakorum
events.summary: The Flemish friar William of Rubruck reaches Möngke's court and spends months at Karakorum. He takes part in a debate between Christians, Muslims and Buddhists held before the khan, and leaves a vivid account of the city.

events.title: Sack of Baghdad
events.summary: Hülegü, Möngke's brother, besieges and sacks Baghdad. The caliph al-Musta'sim is put to death and the Abbasid caliphate ends, a blow long remembered across the Islamic world.

events.title: Möngke dies at Diaoyu Fortress
events.summary: Möngke dies while besieging the Song fortress of Diaoyu, of disease or a wound. His death halts the campaigns in China and the Middle East as the princes go home to fight over the succession.

events.title: Battle of Ain Jalut
events.summary: With most of Hülegü's army withdrawn after Möngke's death, the Mamluks of Egypt under Qutuz and Baybars defeat the Mongol force left in Syria. It is the first major Mongol defeat and stops their advance towards Egypt.

events.title: Kublai proclaimed khan; civil war
events.summary: Kublai is proclaimed Great Khan at Shangdu while his brother Ariq Böke claims the title at Karakorum. Kublai wins the four-year war, but the western khans no longer fully obey him: the empire splits into the Yuan, the Ilkhanate, the Golden Horde and the Chagatai Khanate.

events.title: War between the Golden Horde and the Ilkhanate
events.summary: The first open war between Mongol khanates: Berke of the Golden Horde, a convert to Islam, fights Hülegü of the Ilkhanate over the Caucasus and the sack of Baghdad. Berke allies with the Mamluks, and Hülegü's army is defeated on the frozen Terek River in 1263.

events.title: Siege of Xiangyang
events.place: Xiangyang and Fancheng, on the Han River
events.summary: The Mongols besiege the twin Song cities of Xiangyang and Fancheng for five years. Counterweight trebuchets built by engineers from the Ilkhanate finally break the walls, opening the Yangtze valley to the Mongols.

events.title: Kublai founds the Yuan dynasty
events.summary: Kublai takes the Chinese dynastic name Yuan and rules from Dadu, his new capital on the site of today's Beijing. The Great Khans are now Chinese emperors as well.

events.title: First Mongol invasion of Japan
events.summary: A Mongol and Korean fleet lands at Hakata Bay. After a day of fighting the invaders return to their ships, and a storm wrecks much of the fleet on the way home.

events.title: Marco Polo reaches Kublai's court
events.summary: The Venetian Marco Polo arrives at Shangdu with his father and uncle and stays in Kublai's service for about seventeen years. The book of his travels made the Mongol court famous in Europe.

events.title: Battle of Yamen
events.place: Yamen, at the mouth of the Pearl River
events.summary: In a naval battle in the Pearl River delta the Yuan fleet destroys the last Song forces. A Song minister leaps into the sea with the child emperor, ending the Song dynasty; for the first time all of China is under Mongol rule.

events.title: Second Mongol invasion of Japan
events.summary: A far larger invasion, with fleets from Korea and southern China, is held off by Japanese coastal walls around Hakata. A typhoon, later called the kamikaze or divine wind, then destroys much of the fleet off Takashima.

events.title: Battle of Bạch Đằng
events.summary: On the Bạch Đằng River, the general Trần Hưng Đạo lures the Yuan fleet onto iron-tipped stakes hidden in the riverbed at low tide. The third Mongol invasion of Đại Việt ends in defeat.

events.title: Death of Kublai Khan
events.summary: Kublai dies at Dadu, aged 78, and is succeeded by his grandson Temür. He is the last Great Khan whose authority reached, at least in name, across the whole empire.

events.title: Peace among the khanates
events.place: Agreed between the khans' courts; shown at the Yuan capital, Dadu
events.summary: The khans Temür of the Yuan, Duwa of the Chagatai Khanate, Toqta of the Golden Horde and Öljaitü of the Ilkhanate make peace and recognise the Yuan emperor as their nominal overlord. The truce eases trade and travel along the Silk Road, the period often called the Pax Mongolica.

events.title: Siege of Caffa and the Black Death
events.summary: The Golden Horde under Jani Beg besieges the Genoese port of Caffa. Plague breaks out among the besiegers, and the notary Gabriele de' Mussi wrote that corpses were thrown over the walls. Ships leaving Caffa are thought to have helped carry the Black Death to Europe.

events.title: The Ming take Dadu
events.summary: Ming armies take Dadu, and the last Yuan emperor, Toghon Temür, flees to the steppe. Mongol rule in China ends, though the Northern Yuan keep the title in Mongolia.
